paragraphs: First judge whether you are willing to work long term with definitions, data quality, model assumptions, uncertainty, and rebuttals, rather than only pursuing attractive conclusions.
Positive signal: defines the question and definitions first, then checks the data, method, and alternative explanations.
Caution signal: treating correlation as causation, treating a single significant result as the final answer, or being unwilling to record limitations.

Practice reviewing the seven fields of three fictional research cards: question, data source, sample/scope, period, method, result, review arrangement (uncertainty + escalation target). A: question = change in indicator A; source = dataset A; scope = sample A; period = period A; method = unknown; result = estimate A; review arrangement = record uncertainty and refer the unknown to the research lead, 1 missing. B: question = change in indicator B; source = dataset B; scope = sample B; period = period B; method = unknown; result = estimate B; review arrangement = unknown, 2 missing. C: question = change in indicator C; source = dataset C; scope = sample C; period = period C; method = descriptive comparison; result = estimate C; review arrangement = record uncertainty and refer anomalies to the designated reviewer, 0 missing. Answers 1, 2, 0.
Occupational definition: research economic and statistical data, prepare reports or formulate plans, and address issues such as production and distribution, monetary, or fiscal policy.

entries: Research data in fields such as finance, labor, and agriculture.
Use mathematical models and statistical techniques to explain phenomena and predict trends.
Assess policy impacts and provide consulting on economic relationships.
Inputs: survey, administrative, market, or enterprise data and the institutional context.
Processing: defining indicators, modeling, estimation, validation, and interpretation.
Outputs: reports, charts, forecasts, recommendations, or policy options.
Editorial deliverable suggestion: distinguish descriptive, predictive, and causal questions.
Keep the data dictionary, code, assumptions, and versions.
Deliver uncertainty and limitations together with the conclusions; actual institutional standards are verified separately.

paragraphs: BLS notes that economists also conduct surveys, collect data, and provide advice to businesses, governments, and individuals.
The work is usually done in an office independently or collaboratively, and some positions exceed 40 hours per week.

The U.S. O*NET16 tasks include policy impact, forecasting, consulting, research publication, teaching, and expert testimony; not every position performs all tasks. Education and preparation: the BLS U.S. typical entry requires at least a master's degree, and some government entry positions accept a bachelor's with sufficient economics/statistics/mathematics coursework; business, research, or international organizations may require a master's or doctorate plus work experience. The O*NET new-hire education feedback is 50% master's, 25% doctorate, and 21% bachelor's (the three listed total 96%), which is not a general Chinese education level or recruitment proportion; the Job Zone Five preparation level does not mean that everyone in this occupation has more than five years of experience.
Economists deliver not only models but also explainable conclusions, limitations, and verifiable materials.

Editorial deliverable verification suggestion: the research question, data sources and definitions, method and code, verifiable results, robustness and limitations, and interpretation and recommendations should form a traceable chain, and the real institutional review and release authorization should then be verified; model estimates and final policy value judgments must still be kept separate. This page did not obtain a uniform institutional closed-loop system and is not a general approval process.

19-3011.00 centers on research into economic problems, reports, and policy/market interpretation; it is classified with market research and securities valuation positions by actual main duties. Economists may also analyze consumer demand and sales, so adjacent codes cannot be interpreted as tasks that never overlap.
Economists: explain macroeconomic, policy, or cross-domain economic phenomena and produce research, forecasts, or recommendations.
Market research analysts: study consumers, competition, prices, and marketing conditions to judge the potential sales of a product or service.
Financial and investment analysts: analyze investment projects or institutional financial data and make quantitative judgments such as business valuation.
All three use data, but the research object, end consumer, risk responsibility, and purpose of the recommendations differ, and they cannot be interchanged just because the tools are the same.

Proportions of unique U.S. 2025 postings for this occupation that mention software skills: Excel/R/Python each 27%, PowerPoint18%, SQL15%, and SAS14%; the denominator is all unique postings linked to this O*NET occupation. Editorial candidate, adoption or efficiency for this occupation not verified: test data cleaning code, variable notes, charts, and report drafts on approved materials and check item by item against the raw data.

Editorial candidate, effect not verified: test alternative models, robustness checks, and reproduction checklist drafting; the researcher still verifies the model's applicable assumptions and the code.

The correspondence between variable definitions and the theoretical question requires researcher review; this is a responsibility and quality suggestion, and the task description cannot be used to assert that the technology will never be substitutable.

Causal identification, policy trade-offs, and interest impacts must be reviewed according to the position authority; AI output cannot obtain policy decision-making authority by itself, and no prediction that cannot be automated is made.
Review should return to the raw data, sampling, code, assumptions, estimates, and uncertainty.
Quality looks at reproducibility, robustness, error, consistency of interpretation, and decision consequences, not only generation speed.

Editorial suggestion to compare errors, reproduction, and review time on the same task; no causal evidence of efficiency gains or net employment for this occupation was obtained. Tools do not automatically assume research integrity or policy responsibility.

Fit depends on whether you can connect question definition, data, model, interpretation, and limitations into a reviewable chain.
Positive signal: able to analyze data patterns and proactively look for contrary evidence.
Positive signal: able to explain estimates, charts, and uncertainty to non-specialist readers.
Positive signal: willing to maintain code, a data dictionary, and reproduction records.
Caution signal: chasing only significance without checking the sample, definitions, or model specification.
Caution signal: using complex terminology to cover questions that cannot be answered.
BLS emphasizes analytical, communication, computer, and critical thinking skills.

Editorial observation suggestion: compare whether analysis results can be reproduced and whether limitations can be explained; this round has no evidence that a personality scale predicts work performance, and no judgment of character strengths or weaknesses is made.
Editorial suggestion: verify the data definition, period, and version and explain the differences, and verify the actual data owner and acceptance standards separately.
Editorial suggestion: record the inclusion and exclusion rules, coverage, and key gaps; whether to continue the analysis is determined by the actual project systems.
Editorial suggestion: compare alternative specifications and sensitivity, and when conclusions are unstable mark the limitations and review per the actual systems.
Editorial suggestion: verify the identification assumptions and strength of evidence, and do not write correlation directly as causation; the actual publishing personnel are verified separately.
Editorial suggestion: reproduce the tool code and verify the original citations; the tool cannot obtain release or policy decision-making authority by itself.
